sourcedFrom: F.lli Pietta Black Powder Instruction and Safety Manual (English) — avancarica, English (undated — no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: The Starr is the odd one in Pietta's black powder line: a double action with a take-down bolt and a top frame that tilts forward. Nothing about it matches the Colt or Remington procedures.

steps.title: Never cock this one by hand
steps.action: Before you handle it at all: the Starr must not be manually cocked by the hammer. It is a double action with a secondary trigger, and the manual warns about it in capitals for a reason — cocking it by thumb puts the mechanism somewhere it was not designed to sit. Confirm every chamber is empty and uncapped.
steps.cite: F.lli Pietta Black Powder Instruction and Safety Manual (English) — avancarica, English — ABOUT THE 1858 STARR DOUBLE ACTION REVOLVER, warning, p.23
steps.warn: THE STARR REVOLVER IS UNABLE TO BE MANUALLY COCKED BY THE HAMMER.

steps.title: Clean it after every session
steps.action: Black powder fouling attracts moisture and starts working on the steel as soon as it cools. Pietta makes this an instruction: the gun is cleaned after every shooting session. Glasses on before anything comes apart.
steps.caution: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THE REVOLVER IS COMPLETELY UNLOADED BEFORE CLEANING.
steps.quote: YOUR MUZZLELOADING FIREARM MUST BE CLEANED AFTER EACH SHOOTING SESSION TO PREVENT RUST AND CORROSION FROM DAMAGING THE METAL PARTS.
steps.cite: F.lli Pietta Black Powder Instruction and Safety Manual (English) — avancarica, English — Care and Cleaning, caution, p.29

steps.title: Hammer back to half cock
steps.action: Draw the hammer backward into its half-cock, which is the loading position on this gun. That is where the mechanism has to sit before the take-down bolt will release the frame.
steps.quote: Draw the hammer backward in Half-Cock position (loading position).
steps.cite: F.lli Pietta Black Powder Instruction and Safety Manual (English) — avancarica, English — INITIAL CLEANING PROCEDURE FOR THE STARR REVOLVER, step 1, p.30

steps.title: Take-down bolt unscrewed and removed
steps.action: Unscrew the take-down bolt and take it out. This single fastener is what holds the top frame down — it is the Starr's whole takedown system, and it is why this gun has no wedge and no cylinder pin to pull.
steps.quote: Unscrew and remove the Take-Down Bolt.
steps.cite: F.lli Pietta Black Powder Instruction and Safety Manual (English) — avancarica, English — INITIAL CLEANING PROCEDURE FOR THE STARR REVOLVER, step 2, p.30

steps.title: Tilt the barrel and top frame forward
steps.action: With the bolt out, tilt the barrel and the top frame forward and away from the cylinder. The frame hinges — it does not slide off, and nothing needs driving with a mallet. If it will not move, the take-down bolt is not fully out.
steps.quote: Tilt the barrel and top frame forward away from the cylinder.
steps.cite: F.lli Pietta Black Powder Instruction and Safety Manual (English) — avancarica, English — INITIAL CLEANING PROCEDURE FOR THE STARR REVOLVER, step 3, p.30

steps.title: Trigger eased to drop the cylinder bolt, cylinder out
steps.action: Pull slightly on the trigger to lower the cylinder bolt out of the cylinder, then draw the cylinder gently out. Slightly is the operative word — this is a double action and a full pull does more than lower the bolt. With the bolt down the cylinder lifts free without dragging on it.
steps.quote: Pull slightly on the trigger to lower the cylinder bolt.
steps.cite: F.lli Pietta Black Powder Instruction and Safety Manual (English) — avancarica, English — INITIAL CLEANING PROCEDURE FOR THE STARR REVOLVER, step 4, pp.30-31

steps.title: Grips off the backstrap
steps.action: Take the grips off by removing the screws in the backstrap. That completes the Starr's published strip.
steps.quote: Remove the grips by taking off the screws located in the backstrap.
steps.cite: F.lli Pietta Black Powder Instruction and Safety Manual (English) — avancarica, English — INITIAL CLEANING PROCEDURE FOR THE STARR REVOLVER, step 6, p.31

deepSteps.title: Everything metal, solvent or hot water
deepSteps.action: Clean all the metal parts with a good quality black powder solvent or plenty of hot water. Hot water is a real option on a black powder gun — the fouling dissolves in it and the residual heat helps everything dry. Get into the frame hinge and the bolt seat while the gun is open.
deepSteps.prose: The sentence continues 'solvent or with plenty of hot water.'
deepSteps.quote: Carefully clean all the metal parts with a good quality black powder
deepSteps.cite: F.lli Pietta Black Powder Instruction and Safety Manual (English) — avancarica, English — Care and Cleaning, common procedure, p.29

deepSteps.title: Dry it completely, then oil it lightly
deepSteps.action: Dry every part thoroughly and oil sparingly. Pietta is explicit that heavy oil makes the next session's fouling worse rather than better — on a black powder gun, more oil is not more protection.
deepSteps.quote: Dry all parts thoroughly and lubricate lightly with gun oil. Do not apply the oil heavily as this will contribute to additional fouling during shooting and require more cleaning between shots.
deepSteps.cite: F.lli Pietta Black Powder Instruction and Safety Manual (English) — avancarica, English — Care and Cleaning, common procedure, p.29

deepSteps.title: Reassembly has one order and only one
deepSteps.action: Going back together, seat the REAR of the cylinder in the frame first. Put the front in first and the frame will not close — this instruction exists because the Starr's top frame tilts, and it is the specific failure this gun invites. Ease the trigger to lower the cylinder stop bolt as it goes in so the cylinder is not dragged across it.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ This instruction is the Starr's, not the LeMat's, even though the two procedures share a page. The LeMat has no frame that closes.
deepSteps.quote: Make sure that the rear of the cylinder is seated in the frame first.
deepSteps.cite: F.lli Pietta Black Powder Instruction and Safety Manual (English) — avancarica, English — TO ASSEMBLE THE GUN, step 2, p.31
deepSteps.warn: Do not put the front of the cylinder in first or the frame will not close.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBERS
tasks: Clean the barrel with black powder solvent or plenty of hot water
Clean each chamber of the cylinder the same way
Dry both completely before any oil

cleaning.name: FRAME, HINGE & BOLT
tasks: Clean the frame hinge and the take-down bolt seat while the gun is open
Clean the cylinder stop bolt and its window in the frame
Wipe the recoil shield and the nipple area free of cap fouling

cleaning.name: METAL PARTS GENERALLY
tasks: Carefully clean all the metal parts with a good quality black powder solvent or with plenty of hot water
Dry all parts thoroughly and lubricate lightly with gun oil
Do not apply the oil heavily

reassembly: Reverse the steps in the disassembly section.
Make sure that the rear of the cylinder is seated in the frame first.
Do not put the front of the cylinder in first or the frame will not close.
Gently pull the trigger to lower the cylinder stop bolt so that you will not scratch the cylinder when replacing it in the frame.
fncheck: With the revolver confirmed unloaded and uncapped, check the frame closes fully and the take-down bolt seats, and that the cylinder indexes through the double-action stroke. Do not cock the hammer by hand to test it.
